introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K. Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108.
incertitudes: Points imprimes 2 + (3 + 2) + 3 = 10, conformes au total (les « 3 marks » de 3(c) sont imprimes une seule fois, apres (ii)).

3(b) : les etats imprimes sont « CH3OH(aq) » (probablement (l) dans l'intention du sujet) et un symbole illisible « H2O(2) » lu (l) ; recopie « CH3OH(aq) » tel quel, eau en (l). Le sujet donne DeltaH = -726 kJ/mol pour l'equation ecrite avec 2 mol de methanol ; le diagramme reprend la valeur imprimee sans la modifier. 3(b)(ii) : masse volumique de l'eau 1 g/cm3 supposee (non imprimee).
3(c) : DeltaH = -657 kJ/mol est imprime tel quel (valeur reelle de l'ordre de -65,7 kJ/mol) ; le calcul suit la donnee imprimee, soit 4,83 g.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following.

(i) Exothermic reaction.

(ii) Heat of combustion. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **exothermic reaction** is a reaction in which **heat energy is given out** to the surroundings, so the temperature of the surroundings rises and $\Delta H$ is negative.

(ii) The **heat of combustion** of a substance is the **heat energy (enthalpy change) given out when one mole of the substance burns completely in excess oxygen**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Methanol burns as shown by the following equation:

$2\mathrm{CH_3OH(aq)} + 3\mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO_2(g)} + 4\mathrm{H_2O(l)} \qquad \Delta H = -726\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$

(i) Draw a labelled energy level diagram for this reaction. *[3 marks]*

(ii) When methanol is burnt, the heat evolved is used to raise the temperature of 200 cm$^3$ of water by $25.4^\circ$C. Calculate the heat evolved. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) *What to draw:*

1. A vertical axis labelled **Energy (enthalpy)**, with no numbers needed on the horizontal axis (progress of reaction).
2. A **higher** horizontal line for the reactants, labelled $2\mathrm{CH_3OH} + 3\mathrm{O_2}$.
3. A **lower** horizontal line for the products, labelled $2\mathrm{CO_2} + 4\mathrm{H_2O}$.
4. A **downward arrow** between the two lines labelled $\Delta H = -726$ kJ/mol, showing that the products have less energy than the reactants (heat is given out: exothermic).

(ii) Heat evolved = mass of water $\times$ specific heat capacity $\times$ temperature rise.

Mass of water = 200 cm$^3$ $\times$ 1 g cm$^{-3}$ = 200 g (density of water taken as 1 g cm$^{-3}$).

$Q = 200 \times 4.2 \times 25.4 = 21336\ \mathrm{J} \approx$ **21.3 kJ**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Consider the reaction $\mathrm{Ag^+(aq)} + \mathrm{Cl^-(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{AgCl(s)} \qquad \Delta H = -657\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$

(i) Based on reactants and products only, identify the reaction type.

(ii) What mass of silver chloride, AgCl, would be formed if 22.1 kJ of energy is evolved? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Two aqueous ions combine to give an insoluble solid: it is a **precipitation reaction** (an ionic combination, and exothermic since $\Delta H$ is negative).

(ii) 657 kJ is evolved when 1 mole of AgCl is formed.

Amount of AgCl formed = $\dfrac{22.1}{657} = 0.0336$ mol

Molar mass of AgCl = $108 + 35.5 = 143.5$ g/mol

Mass of AgCl = $0.0336 \times 143.5 \approx$ **4.83 g**
